title: Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact
blurb: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union sign a non-aggression pact with secret protocols to divide Eastern Europe. The diplomatic fuse for Poland is lit.

title: Germany invades Poland
blurb: Without a formal declaration of war, German forces cross into Poland at dawn. Blitzkrieg meets a two-front nightmare when the Soviets invade from the east on the 17th.

title: Britain & France declare war
blurb: Chamberlain’s broadcast ends the illusions of Munich. The European war is official—yet for months the Western Front barely stirs.

title: Soviet invasion of Poland
blurb: The Red Army crosses Poland’s eastern border under the secret pact. Poland is erased between two totalitarian partners.

title: Hitler’s ‘peace’ offer rejected
blurb: After Poland’s fall, Hitler offers a vague ‘peace.’ Britain and France say no. The Phoney War settles in—quiet front, loud propaganda.

title: HMS Royal Oak sunk at Scapa Flow
blurb: U-47 slips into the Home Fleet’s anchorage and sinks a battleship at rest. The Atlantic war will not wait for a Western Front.

title: Winter War begins
blurb: The USSR attacks Finland. Tiny Finnish forces bloody the Red Army through the winter; the peace of March 1940 costs Finland territory but not independence.

title: Battle of the River Plate
blurb: British cruisers corner the pocket battleship Admiral Graf Spee. She limps into Montevideo and is scuttled days later—early Allied naval prestige.

title: First British Empire Empire Air Training graduates
blurb: The British Commonwealth Air Training Plan ramps up. Pilots will be forged far from the Luftwaffe—logistics as strategy.

title: British rationing bites harder
blurb: Bacon, butter and sugar were already ticketed; the coupon book becomes daily life. Fair shares—and black markets—define the home front.

title: Mechelen Incident
blurb: A German plane force-lands with invasion plans for the West. Brussels and Paris are warned; Hitler postpones, then revises. The leak does not save May.

title: Soviet assault on the Mannerheim Line
blurb: After December disasters, the Red Army massively reinforces and pounds Finnish fortifications. The Winter War enters its grinding phase.

title: Altmark Incident
blurb: HMS Cossack boards a German tanker in neutral Norwegian waters and frees Allied POWs. Neutrality frays; Norway’s fate draws nearer.

title: Moscow Peace ends Winter War
blurb: Finland cedes territory but keeps independence. Stalin gets a buffer; Mannerheim’s army becomes legend—and a later co-belligerent against the USSR.

title: Allies debate mining Norwegian waters
blurb: Supreme War Council talks of cutting Sweden’s iron ore route. Plans for Scandinavia collide with Germany’s own—April will decide who moves first.

title: Denmark & Norway invaded
blurb: Weserübung seizes Denmark in hours and contests Norway for two months. The Allies evacuate; Churchill becomes PM mid-crisis.

title: Fall of the Low Countries
blurb: Germany drives through the Ardennes, bypassing the Maginot Line. Rotterdam is bombed; the Netherlands surrender in days.

title: Dunkirk evacuation
blurb: Operation Dynamo lifts ~338,000 Allied troops from the beaches. A military disaster becomes a propaganda deliverance—and Britain fights on.

title: Germans enter Paris
blurb: An open city falls without a fight. The swastika rises over the Eiffel Tower; France’s Third Republic is days from collapse.

title: French armistice
blurb: Hitler forces the signing in the same railway carriage where Germany capitulated in 1918. Vichy governs the unoccupied south; occupation divides France.

title: Battle of Britain begins
blurb: The Luftwaffe tries to smash the RAF ahead of invasion. Radar, fighter production, and pilot skill deny Germany the sky.

title: Adler Tag — Eagle Day
blurb: The Luftwaffe’s planned knockout blow against RAF airfields. Radar, pilots, and production keep Fighter Command alive.

title: ‘Never was so much owed’
blurb: Churchill’s Commons tribute to the Few becomes the war’s most quoted line. Rhetoric as national glue while the sky burns.

title: The Blitz begins
blurb: Night bombing shifts to cities. Fifty-seven consecutive nights hammer London; Coventry, Liverpool, and others burn. Civilian will holds.

title: Italy invades Greece
blurb: Mussolini’s poorly prepared offensive stalls in the mountains. Greek counterattacks push into Albania—drawing German attention south.

title: Taranto — carrier strike
blurb: Swordfish biplanes cripple the Italian battle fleet in harbour. A proof of concept that Japan’s planners will study.

title: Coventry Blitz
blurb: A concentrated night raid gutting the medieval city centre. ‘Coventrate’ enters German propaganda vocabulary; British resolve hardens.

title: Operation Compass opens
blurb: Wavell’s Western Desert Force smashes Italian positions in Egypt. A ‘raid’ becomes a rout across Cyrenaica.

title: Second Great Fire of London
blurb: Incendiaries turn the City into a firestorm on a Sunday night. St Paul’s dome, photographed amid smoke, becomes an icon of endurance.

title: Roosevelt’s Four Freedoms
blurb: State of the Union frames the war as freedom of speech and worship, freedom from want and fear. Soft power for a not-yet-belligerent America.

title: Tobruk falls to the Allies
blurb: Australian and British troops take the port. It will become a siege symbol when Rommel returns.

title: US Lend-Lease debate peaks
blurb: Congress fights over becoming the ‘arsenal of democracy.’ The bill will pass in March—Britain’s supply line politicised and saved.

title: Rommel arrives in Africa
blurb: The Desert Fox lands to stiffen Italian forces. Within weeks the map of Cyrenaica flips again.

title: Lend-Lease becomes law
blurb: Roosevelt signs. Food, fuel, and weapons flow under a legal fiction of ‘lending.’ Neutrality in name only.

title: Yugoslavia signs the Tripartite Pact
blurb: Prince Paul’s government joins the Axis orbit—then a coup in Belgrade days later invites German fury in April.

title: Yugoslavia & Greece invaded
blurb: Germany overruns Yugoslavia in days and Greece soon after. Crete falls by air in May—costly for German paratroops.

title: Hess flies to Scotland
blurb: Deputy Führer parachutes in with a private ‘peace’ fantasy. Berlin calls him mad; London locks him up. A bizarre sideshow before Barbarossa.

title: Battle of Crete begins
blurb: German airborne assault seizes the island at brutal cost to Fallschirmjäger. Hitler never tries a comparable drop again.

title: Hood sunk — Bismarck chase
blurb: Bismarck destroys HMS Hood in minutes. The Royal Navy’s revenge hunt ends with Bismarck down on the 27th.

title: Operation Barbarossa
blurb: Three million Axis troops smash into the Soviet Union—the largest land invasion in history. Stalin is stunned; the character of the war turns genocidal in the East.

title: Anglo-Soviet agreement
blurb: Mutual assistance against Germany—awkward partners united by necessity. Convoys to Murmansk will follow.

title: Göring orders the ‘Final Solution’ prep
blurb: A bureaucratic directive tasks Heydrich with an overall plan. Mass murder in the East is already underway; Wannsee will coordinate it. Sober, not a game piece.

title: Atlantic Charter
blurb: Churchill and Roosevelt draft postwar ideals aboard warships: no aggrandisement, free trade, self-determination. A prospectus for the UN world.

title: Kiev pocket forming
blurb: Hitler prioritises the southern encirclement over the direct Moscow drive. Hundreds of thousands of Soviet troops will be trapped by September.

title: Siege of Leningrad begins
blurb: The city is cut off. Nearly 900 days of starvation, cold, and shelling follow—one of the war’s longest and cruelest sieges.

title: Kiev falls
blurb: The Wehrmacht completes a vast encirclement. Hundreds of thousands of Soviet troops are captured—and the road opens toward further atrocity in Ukraine.

title: Drive on Moscow (Typhoon)
blurb: Operation Typhoon aims to take the Soviet capital before winter. Mud, then frost, then a Soviet reserve army will stop it.

title: Operation Crusader
blurb: Eighth Army drives to relieve Tobruk. Chaotic tank battles; Rommel eventually falls back—Tobruk free for now.

title: Rostov changes hands
blurb: Germans take the city, then Soviet counterattacks force the first major Wehrmacht withdrawal of the eastern campaign.

title: Soviet Moscow counteroffensive
blurb: Fresh Siberian divisions and winter smash the frozen German spearheads. The myth of Wehrmacht invincibility cracks.

title: Germany declares war on the US
blurb: Four days after Pearl Harbor, Hitler declares war on the United States—bringing American industry fully into the European struggle.

title: Wannsee Conference
blurb: Senior Nazi officials coordinate the logistics of the ‘Final Solution.’ This site treats the Holocaust soberly and separately from campaign scrubbing—see the note in About.

title: Albert Speer becomes Armaments Minister
blurb: After Todt’s death, Speer inherits the war economy. German production will rise even as the strategic picture darkens—slave labour included.

title: Singapore falls
blurb: Outside Europe’s map, but it shakes London: Britain’s eastern fortress surrenders. Churchill calls it the worst disaster in British military history.

title: RAF Bomber Command’s area-bombing directive era
blurb: Night area attacks on German cities intensify under Harris’s rising influence. Ethics and effectiveness will be argued for decades.

title: St Nazaire Raid
blurb: Commandos ram HMS Campbeltown into the Normandie dry dock and wreck it. Costly; the only Atlantic dock for capital ships is denied to Tirpitz.

title: Doolittle Raid (echo in Europe)
blurb: US bombers hit Japan from a carrier—news that stiffens Allied morale worldwide even as Europe waits for a second front.

title: Baedeker Blitz begins
blurb: Luftwaffe retaliatory raids on historic English towns after RAF hits Lübeck and Rostock. Culture as target.

title: Rommel drives on Egypt
blurb: The Desert Fox breaks the Gazala line; Tobruk falls in June. Egypt—and the Suez—suddenly look reachable.

title: Midway (global hinge)
blurb: Not on the Europe map—but the Pacific turn matters to London and Berlin’s calendars. Japan’s carrier elite is gutted.

title: Lidice destroyed
blurb: After Heydrich’s assassination, the village is erased—men shot, women and children deported. Terror as policy. Treated soberly here.

title: Tobruk falls to Rommel
blurb: A shock surrender. Churchill, in Washington, takes the blow; Egypt suddenly looks open.

title: Battle of Stalingrad opens
blurb: House-by-house fighting begins on the Volga. What starts as a city fight becomes the war’s decisive German catastrophe.

title: Dieppe Raid
blurb: A costly Allied reconnaissance-in-force on the French coast. Lessons in landing craft, armor, and air cover will shape Normandy.

title: Gandhi’s Quit India echoes in London
blurb: August’s mass movement in India keeps Whitehall sweating over imperial legitimacy while the desert and Volga burn.

title: Stalingrad street fighting intensifies
blurb: Chuikov’s 62nd Army clings to Volga rubble. Every block costs a company; the city becomes a meat grinder.

title: Second El Alamein
blurb: Montgomery’s Eighth Army breaks Rommel. Churchill: ‘Before Alamein we never had a victory. After Alamein we never had a defeat.’

title: Operation Torch
blurb: American and British forces land in French North Africa. Vichy resistance fades; the Axis is soon squeezed from east and west.

title: Operation Uranus
blurb: Soviet pincers smash through weak Romanian flanks and encircle the German Sixth Army. The trap closes.

title: UN declaration on Jewish mass murder
blurb: Allies publicly condemn the Nazi extermination program. Knowledge is no longer deniable; rescue still lags. Sober entry.

title: Operation Winter Storm fails
blurb: Manstein’s relief drive toward the pocket stalls. Sixth Army’s fate is sealed short of Christmas miracles.

title: Casablanca Conference
blurb: Roosevelt and Churchill demand unconditional surrender and map the Sicily path. Stalin isn’t there—still the eastern butcher’s bill speaks loudest.

title: First USAAF heavy raid on Germany
blurb: American daylight doctrine arrives over the Reich. Escort gaps will bloody the 8th Air Force before long-range fighters mature.

title: Sixth Army surrenders
blurb: Field Marshal Paulus capitulates. Roughly 90,000 Axis troops march into captivity; maybe 5–6,000 ever see home. The strategic initiative in the East passes to the USSR.

title: Goebbels’ Total War speech
blurb: At the Sportpalast, Goebbels asks ‘Do you want total war?’ The crowd roars yes. Propaganda tries to paper over Stalingrad.

title: Battle of the Bismarck Sea
blurb: Allied air power annihilates a Japanese convoy—another Pacific datapoint that Allied industrial air supremacy is transferable.

title: Battle of the Ruhr opens
blurb: Bomber Command’s campaign against Germany’s industrial heartland. Dams Raid will punctuate May; the cities burn for months.

title: First major Smersh/plot talk — Hitler nearly bombed
blurb: Officers’ resistance circles keep trying; a bomb on Hitler’s plane fails to detonate. July 1944 will be the near-miss that gets into textbooks.

title: Boulter / Voskhod — Atlantic convoy crisis eases
blurb: May will be ‘Black May’ for U-boats; by spring 1943 escort carriers, Huff-Duff, and centimetric radar are winning the tonnage war.

title: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
blurb: Jewish fighters resist the final deportation. The ghetto is razed; the rising becomes a symbol of defiance amid genocide. Sober.

title: Axis surrender in Tunisia
blurb: A quarter-million Axis troops lay down arms. Africa is cleared; the Mediterranean becomes an Allied highway toward Sicily.

title: Pantelleria surrenders
blurb: An island pounded into surrender largely by air—prelude to Husky. Mussolini’s empire shrinks to the mainland and nerves.

title: Race riot / Zoot Suit echoes reach Allied press
blurb: US home-front racial violence (Zoot Suit / Detroit) is reported abroad. Democracies at war still fail their own ideals—lesson, not decoration.

title: Battle of Kursk
blurb: The largest tank battle in history. Germany’s last major strategic offensive in the East dies in Soviet defenses and counterstrokes.

title: Allies invade Sicily
blurb: Husky lands Anglo-American forces on Sicily. Within weeks Mussolini is deposed; Italy’s Fascist regime cracks.

title: Sicily secured — Messina taken
blurb: Allies finish the island; many Axis troops escape to the mainland. Mussolini is already gone; Italy’s surrender talks accelerate.

title: Schweinfurt–Regensburg raids
blurb: Deep USAAF strikes on ball-bearing plants without adequate escort. Losses are staggering; daylight strategy is forced to rethink.

title: Quebec Conference (Quadrant)
blurb: Overlord planning firms up; South-East Asia command reshuffles. The second front gets a calendar.

title: Allies land in mainland Italy
blurb: Italy surrenders; Germany seizes the north and digs in. Salerno is nearly thrown back into the sea. A long, bitter slog up the peninsula begins.

title: Naples rises and is liberated
blurb: Four Days of Naples: civilians fight Germans before Allied entry. The city’s port will feed the Italian campaign.

title: Italy declares war on Germany
blurb: The Badoglio government switches sides. German occupation of the north hardens; civil war layers onto the campaign.

title: Tehran Conference
blurb: Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin meet. Overlord is locked in for 1944; the shape of the postwar world starts to be bargained.

title: Bari mustard-gas disaster
blurb: A Luftwaffe raid hits a ship secretly carrying Allied chemical munitions. Secrecy first; medical lessons later. Ugly logistics of deterrence.

title: Scharnhorst sunk at North Cape
blurb: Royal Navy battleship Duke of York and escorts kill Germany’s last major fleet threat to Arctic convoys in a polar night fight.

title: Anzio landing
blurb: A flanking landing meant to break the Gustav Line stalls into a bloody beachhead. Rome will wait until June.

title: Leningrad siege lifted
blurb: After 872 days, the corridor opens for good. The human cost is almost beyond measure—estimates near a million civilian dead.

title: Monte Cassino abbey bombed
blurb: Allied bombers smash the medieval monastery—wrongly thought to be a German OP. The ruins become better defences. Culture destroyed for little gain.

title: Big Week — Argument
blurb: Concentrated USAAF attacks on Luftwaffe production and, crucially, attrition of German fighters. Air superiority for Overlord is being bought.

title: Third Battle of Monte Cassino
blurb: New Zealand and Indian troops grind into the town. The Gustav Line still holds; spring will need a fresh plan.

title: The Great Escape
blurb: Allied airmen tunnel out; most are recaptured, fifty murdered on Hitler’s order. Wartime legend with a body count.

title: Ploiești oil under renewed attack
blurb: Fifteenth Air Force hammers Axis fuel. Oil, not just factories, becomes the strategic target set.

title: Exercise Tiger disaster
blurb: D-Day rehearsal hit by E-boats; hundreds of US troops die. Kept quiet lest Overlord’s calendar slip.

title: Crimea cleared — Sevastopol retaken
blurb: Soviet armies finish the Crimean offensive. German 17th Army wrecked; the Black Sea map flips.

title: Monte Cassino finally falls
blurb: Polish II Corps raises its flag over the ruins. The road toward Rome opens—just in time for headlines to be stolen by Normandy.

title: Allies enter Rome
blurb: The first Axis capital falls—two days before Normandy steals the headlines. German forces withdraw in good order to the Gothic Line.

title: D-Day — Normandy landings
blurb: Overlord: five beaches, airborne drops, the greatest amphibious assault ever mounted. A foothold in Fortress Europe is won by nightfall—at terrible cost on Omaha.

title: Operation Bagration
blurb: On the anniversary of Barbarossa, the Red Army annihilates Army Group Centre. The map of the East rewrites itself in weeks.

title: July 20 plot
blurb: Stauffenberg’s bomb fails to kill Hitler. The purge that follows guts the conservative resistance inside the Wehrmacht.

title: Warsaw Uprising
blurb: The Polish Home Army rises as the Red Army nears. Stalin’s forces halt across the Vistula; the city is destroyed over 63 days.

title: Invasion of southern France
blurb: Operation Dragoon races up the Rhône. German Army Group G retreats; France is liberated from two directions.

title: Liberation of Paris
blurb: French 2nd Armored and US forces enter; Resistance rises. De Gaulle walks the Champs-Élysées. The city’s cultural weight makes the moment electric.

title: Market Garden
blurb: A bridge too far. Ambitious airborne thrusts into the Netherlands fail to seize the Rhine crossing at Arnhem.

title: Warsaw Uprising ends
blurb: After 63 days, Home Army survivors surrender. The city is systematically destroyed; Soviet forces had stayed across the river.

title: Rommel forced to suicide
blurb: Implied July Plot links: choose poison, get a state funeral. The regime eats its own legend.

title: Belgrade liberated
blurb: Soviet and Yugoslav Partisan forces take the capital. The Balkans unravel westward.

title: Aachen falls
blurb: First German city taken by the Western Allies. Urban fighting preview for what waits deeper in the Reich.

title: Battle of Leyte Gulf (global)
blurb: Largest naval battle; Japanese surface fleet effectively finished. Europe’s map doesn’t move—Tokyo’s options collapse.

title: FDR wins fourth term
blurb: Wartime America re-elects Roosevelt. Continuity of Allied leadership—until April’s shock.

title: Tirpitz sunk
blurb: Lancasters with Tallboys finally kill the lonely battleship. The ‘fleet in being’ that pinned British capital ships is gone.

title: Operation Queen — Hurtgen continues
blurb: US push toward the Roer stalls in dense woods and minefields. A meat-grinder often overshadowed by the Bulge next door.

title: Battle of the Bulge
blurb: Hitler’s last major western offensive punches a salient through thin US lines. Bastogne holds; fuel and air power decide the rest.

title: Vistula–Oder offensive
blurb: Zhukov and Konev surge from the Vistula to the Oder in two weeks—stopping 70 km from Berlin. East Prussia is cut off.

title: Yalta Conference
blurb: The Big Three carve occupation zones and argue Poland’s future. The Cold War’s outline is visible if you squint.

title: Dresden firebombed
blurb: RAF and USAAF raids create a firestorm in a crowded refugee city. The morality of area bombing remains bitterly contested.

title: Remagen bridge seized
blurb: US troops find the Ludendorff Bridge still standing and cross the Rhine. A temporary miracle accelerates the western advance.

title: Battle of Berlin begins
blurb: Soviet armies assault the capital. Street fighting, Hitler’s bunker, and the final collapse of Nazi authority follow.

title: Elbe Day — link-up
blurb: US and Soviet patrols meet on the Elbe. Germany is cut in two; photographers stage the handshake for history.

title: Hitler dead
blurb: Hitler suicides as Soviet troops close on the Reich Chancellery. Dönitz inherits a wreck for a few days of ‘government.’

title: Berlin falls
blurb: The Berlin garrison surrenders. The Red Banner over the Reichstag becomes the iconic image of victory in Europe.

title: German surrender signed
blurb: Jodl signs unconditional surrender at Eisenhower’s HQ. A second ceremony in Berlin follows; VE Day is celebrated on the 8th (and the 9th in Moscow).

title: VE Day
blurb: Crowds fill Whitehall and the Champs-Élysées. The European war is over. The Pacific war—and the atomic age—still wait.
